title: GPU exhaustion follow-up: graded fallbacks, queue-debounce, and telemetry mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-08 we observed a hosted API capacity exhaustion event that manifested as progressive queue buildup, request throttling, and degraded p99 tail latency. Initial mitigation (manual slot priming and aggressive eviction) restored capacity but surfaced recurring regressions when cold KV-cache churn coincided with tenant prefetch bursts. Root cause analysis points to three interacting issues: (1) a small number of large tenants triggering long-running prefetches that pinned slot capacity, (2) KV cache pollution causing amplification of sequence-length and memory pressure, and (3) an autoscaler hysteresis/soft-start configuration that delayed additional GPU provisioning during fast surges. This ticket tracks the follow-ups and action items to reduce recurrence risk, harden telemetry, and provide safe automated fallbacks.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Triage: Incident review with SRE, Runtime, and Capacity teams. Agreed to split immediate mitigations vs medium-term changes. Action: enable priority-based slot caps for top 20 tenants (owner: Miguel Santos).

2026-03-11 — Investigation: Found correlation between tenant prefetch jobs (long-decoder sequences) and KV-cache thrash. Proposed short-term: limit prefetch concurrency + conservative cache eviction policy. (owner: Lina Chen)

2026-03-12 — Design decision: Implement 'queue-debounce' admission control—delay admitting low-priority prefetch requests when queue slope > 0.6 for 20s. Trade-off: slight added latency for warmup traffic vs preventing cascade queue growth. Approved by Runtime leads.

2026-03-12 — Fallback plan: Add graded fallback chain: (A) quantized model variant on same pool, (B) route to dedicated burst pool with trimmed sequence-length, (C) degrade to cached completion if available. This keeps requests served with graceful degradation rather than hard rejects. (owner: Priya Raman)

2026-03-13 — Telemetry: Missing signal discovered — no reliable 'queue slope' metric in Alerting. PagerDuty alerts will be gated on p95 queue-slope and p99 slot-occupancy. Dashboards updated (link below). (owner: DataDog team)
2026-03-13 — PR opened for gate: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3721 — implements queue-debounce and tenant-concurrency caps. Seeking review from Ivan and Mei.

2026-03-14 — Interim rollout: feature gated via runtime flags; staged rollout to 10% of clusters for two days to validate no regression on low-latency tenants. Metrics to watch: request success rate, p99 latency, slot churn rate.
